newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to allow imports of disease-free Taiwan pork.
newsitem.headline: Japan to allow imports of disease-free Taiwan pork.

text.p: Japan's Agriculture Ministry said on Thursday it will allow imports of some Taiwan pork slaughtered before February 20 and shipped before March 18, but ruled out any immediate easing of the import ban.

"Taiwan pork can be imported into Japan, as long as it meets these requirements," a ministry official said. "There's no reason to ban imports of disease-free pork." He could not say how many tonnes of Taiwan pork are likely to meet the requirements.
On March 21, the Agriculture Ministry indefinitely banned all pork imports from Taiwan, its largest supplier, due to an outbreak of the highly contagious foot and mouth disease there.
Japan is the largest export market of Taiwanese pork. It imported 653,176 tonnes of pork in 1996, the Finance Ministry said. Of that, 266,225 tonnes, 40.7 percent, came from Taiwan.

Taiwan and Japan held talks on the pork import ban earlier this week and Taiwanese side called for easing of import ban. "But we have no plan to ease import ban at the moment," the ministry official said. -- Tokyo Commodities Desk (+81-3-3432-7391)
